findings.location: source.html — Scripture quotations (Acts 24:25; Acts 26:24; Romans 1:20; Jeremiah 31:35-36; 2 Peter 3:4; Isaiah 55:8-9; Psalm 14:1; Psalm 8:3-4; Acts 17:28; 2 Timothy 3:7)
findings.source_quote: All scripture quotations in the English source are given in contemporary English (e.g. “Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time… –Acts 24:25.”; “Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad –Acts 26:24.”; “For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen… –Romans 1:20.” etc.)
findings.suggested_fix: Translate every quoted Scripture passage into contemporary Modern Greek (not Koine/Ancient Greek). Preserve the exact verse numbers, ranges and their placement, and preserve italics/emphasis as in the source HTML. Use commonly accepted Modern Greek Bible phrasing (or an established Modern Greek translation) that conveys the printed English meaning, but do not insert or remove references or change verse numbering. For example: • Acts 24:25 — render in Modern Greek: «…έτσι δίδαξε περί δικαιοσύνης, εγκράτειας και κρίσεως ερχόμενης…» followed by «Ο Φήλιξ σείστηκε και είπε: Πορεύου· και άλλη φορά, όταν θα έχω ευκαιρία, θα σε καλέσω. — Πράξεις 24:25.» • Acts 26:24 — use a Modern Greek idiom: «…ο Φέστος είπε με δυνατή φωνή: Παῦλε, έχεις παραληρήσει· η πολλή μάθησις σε έχει οδηγήσει σε τρέλα. — Πράξεις 26:24.» • Romans 1:20 and other quoted verses — replace the current Koine-style Greek with contemporary Modern Greek renderings (e.g. Romans 1:20: «Διότι τα αόρατα του Θεού, από τη δημιουργία του κόσμου, γίνονται ευκρινώς αντιληπτά μέσα στα έργα του — την αιώνια δύναμη και θεότητα του — ώστε να μην έχουν δικαιολογία. — Ρωμαίους 1:20.»). Apply the same approach to Jeremiah 31:35-36; 2 Peter 3:4; Isaiah 55:8-9; Psalm 14:1; Psalm 8:3-4; Acts 17:28; 2 Timothy 3:7. Keep HTML tags and emphasized text as in the translation. This will align the translation with the requested contemporary Modern Greek target language and the project's instruction to render quoted Scripture in the target language.
findings.translation_quote: The translator rendered the quoted Scriptures mostly in Koine/ancient-style Greek (examples: Acts 26:24 as “Παῦλε, σὺ παράφυος εἶ· πολλή μάθησις σε τρέλλαν εποιεῖ”, Romans 1:20 as “ὅτι τὰ ἀόρατα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ κτίσεως κόσμου… – Ρωμαίους 1:20.”, Jeremiah 31:35-36 and others similarly in non-contemporary forms).

findings.source_quote: English source: “...Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad –Acts 26:24.”
findings.suggested_fix: Use a natural, contemporary Modern Greek rendering for the quoted line so it reads idiomatically to modern readers. For example: «…ο Φέστος είπε με δυνατή φωνή: “Παύλε, έχεις παραληρήσει — η πολλή μάθηση σε έχει οδηγήσει σε τρέλα.” — Πράξεις 26:24.» Replace the current archaizing/Koine phrasing (e.g. “παράφυος”) with the suggested Modern Greek wording, preserving verse number and emphasis tags.
findings.translation_quote: Current translation uses an archaic / Koine phrasing: “Παῦλε, σὺ παράφυος εἶ· πολλή μάθησις σε τρέλλαν εποιεῖ – Πράξεις 26:24.”
